headline: Shock exit: Julian Nagelsmann resigns as Germany coach after World Cup crash
summary: The 38-year-old steps down following a last-32 exit to Paraguay, with Jurgen Klopp emerging as the preferred replacement.
details: Julian Nagelsmann has resigned as the head coach of the German national team following a shock last-32 exit from the World Cup at the hands of Paraguay.
Reports from Bild and Sky Germany indicate that Nagelsmann accepted the German Football Federation's (DFB) request for him to step down, despite being under contract until 2028.
The 38-year-old was reportedly offered a seven million euro ($8 million) severance package, roughly one year's salary, during a three-hour meeting at DFB headquarters in Frankfurt.
Germany's exit was marked by a penalty shootout loss to Paraguay in Boston, the first time the team has ever lost on penalties in a World Cup.
Nagelsmann becomes the second national coach in German history to be sacked after predecessor Hansi Flick suffered the same fate in 2023.
The DFB's preferred candidate to take over is believed to be former Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp, who currently serves as Red Bull's global head of football.
Klopp, a highly popular figure in Germany, is said to have a release clause that would allow him to return to the national team role.
caption:
A shock World Cup exit leads to a major shakeup. Julian Nagelsmann is out as Germany's head coach.

Julian Nagelsmann has resigned as the head coach of the German national team following a shock last-32 exit from the World Cup at the hands of Paraguay.

Reports from Bild and Sky Germany indicate that Nagelsmann accepted the German Football Federation's (DFB) request for him to step down, despite being under contract until 2028.

The 38-year-old was reportedly offered a seven million euro ($8 million) severance package, roughly one year's salary, during a three-hour meeting at DFB headquarters in Frankfurt.

Germany's exit was marked by a penalty shootout loss to Paraguay in Boston, the first time the team has ever lost on penalties in a World Cup.

Nagelsmann becomes the second national coach in German history to be sacked after predecessor Hansi Flick suffered the same fate in 2023.

The DFB's preferred candidate to take over is believed to be former Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp, who currently serves as Red Bull's global head of football.

Klopp, a highly popular figure in Germany, is said to have a release clause that would allow him to return to the national team role.

headline_marked: Speaker Hafiz Uddin [[condemns killing of Iran's Supreme Leader]] in Tehran
headline: Speaker Hafiz Uddin condemns killing of Iran's Supreme Leader in Tehran
summary: National Parliament Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad leads a Bangladesh delegation to the state funeral of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, expressing solidarity with the people of Iran.
details: National Parliament Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad has expressed profound condolences and condemned the brutal killing of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
Leading a Bangladesh delegation to Tehran, the Speaker met with Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, speaker of the Islamic Consultative Assembly of Iran, to pay his respects.
During the meeting, the two leaders discussed the centuries-old friendship and deep cultural and people-to-people ties between Bangladesh and Iran.
Speaker Hafiz Uddin appreciated the constructive role of his Iranian counterpart in facilitating a recent peace memorandum of understanding (MoU) between Iran and the United States.
He expressed hope that the agreement will bring lasting peace, stability, and prosperity to the Iranian people and the wider region.
The Speaker reaffirmed Bangladesh's support for the ongoing peace process and urged all parties to use dialogue and diplomacy to resolve outstanding issues.
The Bangladesh delegation was received at the airport by Hamid Reza Haji Babaei, deputy speaker of the Islamic Consultative Assembly of Iran.
caption:
Bangladesh's National Parliament Speaker condemns the brutal killing of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei while attending his state funeral in Tehran.

National Parliament Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad has expressed profound condolences and condemned the brutal killing of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

Leading a Bangladesh delegation to Tehran, the Speaker met with Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, speaker of the Islamic Consultative Assembly of Iran, to pay his respects.

During the meeting, the two leaders discussed the centuries-old friendship and deep cultural and people-to-people ties between Bangladesh and Iran.

Speaker Hafiz Uddin appreciated the constructive role of his Iranian counterpart in facilitating a recent peace memorandum of understanding (MoU) between Iran and the United States.

He expressed hope that the agreement will bring lasting peace, stability, and prosperity to the Iranian people and the wider region.

The Speaker reaffirmed Bangladesh's support for the ongoing peace process and urged all parties to use dialogue and diplomacy to resolve outstanding issues.

The Bangladesh delegation was received at the airport by Hamid Reza Haji Babaei, deputy speaker of the Islamic Consultative Assembly of Iran.
